profile.name: Zeyi Zhang
profile.headline: Ph.D. Candidate in Chemistry, UC Berkeley
profile.bio: I develop quantum chemistry and AI methods to make molecular simulation more predictive and practical. My work combines electronic-structure theory, GPU computing, and machine learning to study excited states, strong correlation, and chemical transformations. I develop PARSEC.py, contribute to Q-Chem, and build scientific benchmarks and agentic workflows that connect simulations with spectroscopy. Applications include interfacial chemistry, CO₂ capture, and microelectronics. I am a Ph.D. candidate in theoretical chemistry at UC Berkeley, advised by Prof. Martin Head-Gordon and Dr. Jin Qian, and a Graduate Student Researcher at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. I am also a Research Scientist Intern at ByteDance Seed–AI for Science.
research_interests: Spectroscopy, reaction chemistry, and materials applications

projects.name: GPU-accelerated quantum chemistry
projects.summary: Develop ByteQC and GPU4PySCF with tensor hypercontraction (THC) for HF, perturbation, and CC theory, reducing average runtime and GPU memory by 38% and 72% on A100 GPUs.
projects.homepage_summary: GPU algorithms for Hartree–Fock and correlated electronic-structure calculations in ByteQC and GPU4PySCF.

projects.name: Transition-metal data generation
projects.summary: Develop JaQMC for transition-metal data generation via auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC), yielding a Cr₂ curve closer to experiment than DMRG and 9.5% lower BDE MAE than MRCC.
projects.homepage_summary: Auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo reference data for transition-metal systems using JaQMC.

projects.name: Machine-learned DFT
projects.summary: Explore training methods for machine-learned density functional theory (MLDFT).

experience.homepage_summary: GPU-accelerated quantum chemistry with THC; AFQMC reference data for transition metals; exploration of MLDFT training methods.

projects.name: PARSEC.py
projects.summary: Develop a Python-based real-space Kohn–Sham DFT code with ML density interfaces, multi-node/multi-GPU parallelization, and GPU-accelerated geometry optimization and molecular dynamics.

details.text: Integrate ML density models like ChargE3Net and SCDP, reducing SCF iterations by up to 26.7%.
Converge DFT for a system with over 10,000 atoms (~40,000 valence electrons) in under 5 minutes on 16 A100 GPUs.
Interface with ML force fields like UMA and MACE, reducing total relaxation time by up to 48%.
Investigate X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, interfacial chemistry, and CO₂ capture.

projects.homepage_summary: A GPU-accelerated real-space DFT code with machine-learned charge densities and multi-GPU support.

projects.name: State-Specific Excited-State Theories, Multireference Methods, and Strong Correlation
projects.summary: Develop electronic-structure methods for excited states and strongly correlated systems.

details.text: Develop energy decomposition analysis for excitations in two-determinant ROKS.
Develop a frozen MO initial guess for orbital-optimized DFT of charge-transfer excitations.
Study strongly correlated C₂ with HF, DFT, and multireference NOCI(-RSPT) versus MRCI+Q and experiment, achieving 32%/24% lower bond-length/energy MAEs than EOM-DIP-CCSD for low-lying states.

projects.homepage_summary: Electronic-structure methods for excited states and strongly correlated systems.

projects.summary: Develop machine-learned models for electronic states and molecular properties.

Develop an electronic force field by considering orbital response in non-self-consistent MLH.
Develop manifold-based flow-matching models for electronic states and molecular properties.

publications.title: MolP2SBench: Do LLMs Really Reason from Molecular Properties to Structure?

image.alt: MolP2SBench workflow and property interventions for molecular structure reasoning.

publications.summary: MolP2SBench evaluates how LLMs infer molecular structure from physical properties. By testing their reliance on the supplied evidence and their responses to changes in that evidence, it reveals strengths and limitations in property-grounded molecular reasoning.

publications.title: On Policy Self Distillation for Learning Kohn-Sham Hamiltonian.

image.alt: On-policy self-distillation learns Hamiltonians from dense SCF corrections.

publications.summary: OPSD uses the self-consistent-field solver as a teacher for pretrained Hamiltonian models, turning corrections to their own predictions into learning signals. This iterative self-distillation improves accuracy and transferability while reducing dependence on costly reference calculations.

publications.title: PARSEC.py: A Python-Based Real-Space Kohn–Sham Density Functional Theory Code Accelerated by Machine Learned Charge Density.

image.alt: Real-space grid representation of a molecule and the sparsity pattern of its Kohn–Sham Hamiltonian; graphical abstract from the Real-space KS-DFT review.

publications.summary: PARSEC.py combines real-space Kohn–Sham DFT and machine-learned charge-density initialization in a modular Python framework. Molecular benchmarks show fewer self-consistent-field iterations with suitable density guesses, while GPU acceleration speeds up diagonalization and Hartree-potential calculations.

publications.title: Ionization-Driven Oxygen–Oxygen Bond Formation in Mixed CO₂–H₂O Clusters: The Role of Solvation and Cluster Composition.

image.alt: Reaction pathways and ion products following photoionization of mixed carbon dioxide–water clusters, including oxygen–oxygen bond formation and hydrogen peroxide products.

publications.summary: Photoionization experiments and density functional theory reveal how local hydration controls oxygen–oxygen bond formation in CO₂–H₂O clusters. Water-rich environments favor peroxide-forming reactions, while molecular rearrangement and evaporation provide an indirect route to hydrogen peroxide.

publications.title: An Energy Decomposition Method for Electronic Excitations in Two-Determinant Restricted Open-Shell Kohn–Sham Theory.

image.alt: ROKS-EDA schematic connecting a ROKS orbital occupation diagram to OVOCV orbital and NOCV density-difference visualizations.

publications.summary: An energy decomposition framework for two-determinant ROKS excited states separates primary excitation from orbital relaxation. By quantifying energy changes and charge redistribution through orbital analysis, it helps interpret valence, core, and charge-transfer excitations.

publications.title: An Improved Guess for the Variational Calculation of Charge-transfer Excitations in Large Systems.

image.alt: Freeze-and-release squared-gradient minimization for charge-transfer excitations in a donor–acceptor cage.

publications.summary: A freeze-and-release scheme combines constrained initial guesses with squared-gradient minimization for orbital-optimized DFT. Tests on a supramolecular coordination cage and dye–semiconductor complexes demonstrate convergence to targeted charge-transfer excited states while avoiding collapse to lower-energy states.

publications.title: Real-space Kohn–Sham Density Functional Theory for Complex Energy Applications.

image.alt: Figures 6, 8 and 9: carbonate at the air–water interface, wood-derived carbon capture, and carbon dioxide on graphene.

publications.summary: This review examines the foundations and computational advances of real-space Kohn–Sham DFT, with applications to interfacial spectroscopy and carbon capture. It discusses opportunities for large-scale electronic-structure simulations alongside current limitations and future directions for exascale computing.
